lessons.title: Review — one arrow
lessons.gloss: review — one arrow, two directions, and the phrases you already owned lined up under it

needs: your eyes, because the lesson points at something written down
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your eyes, so it is not fully a driving lesson. You will want your eyes, because the lesson points at something written down. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: Nothing new. One question before the table: which way does each preposition point?

utterances: built from. para — toward: ad, "toward". por — through, because: per, "through".
the arrow. para — toward: points at it. por — through, because: comes from it.
a person. para — toward: para ti — you get it. por — through, because: por ti — you caused it.
a time. para — toward: para mañana — by then. por — through, because: —.
thanks. para — toward: —. por — through, because: gracias por — for what caused it.
asking. para — toward: —. por — through, because: por favor — through a favour.
asking why. para — toward: —. por — through, because: ¿por qué? — through what?

segments.text: Look at the right-hand column. Four of those six por entries are phrases you have owned since the opening chapters. This review is not mostly teaching you new Spanish — it is re-filing old Spanish under a heading that explains it.
That happens more than a course usually admits. A great deal of what looks like new grammar late in a book is a name for something you have been doing correctly and blindly for a long time.

blocks.title: Grammar Lens: what to do when you are unsure

segments.text: You will still hesitate sometimes. Two things help, in this order:
Ask what the sentence is about. A destination, a deadline, a recipient, a purpose — para. A cause, a route, a swap, a duration — por.
If it is genuinely both, it is genuinely both. Lo hago para ti and lo hago por ti are both good Spanish; you are not choosing right from wrong, you are choosing which thing to say.

That second point matters more than it looks. Most por/para anxiety comes from believing every sentence has one correct answer waiting to be found. Plenty of sentences take either, and the choice is the meaning.

segments.instruction: "para ti / por ti", "para mañana", "gracias por la comida"
segments.source: [YOU SAY: "para ti / por ti", "para mañana", "gracias por la comida"]

segments.prompt: Give the two directions in one line.
acceptedResponses: para points at it, por comes from it
para toward, por through or because

feedback.incorrect: Para points at the thing; por comes from it.

segments.prompt: Name three phrases you already knew that turn out to contain por.
acceptedResponses: por favor, por que, gracias por

feedback.incorrect: por favor, ¿por qué?, porque, gracias por — any three.

segments.prompt: A sentence takes either por or para. What should you conclude?
acceptedResponses: that it means two different things
both are correct and the choice is the meaning

feedback.correct: Not right versus wrong — which thing you are saying.
feedback.incorrect: That both are good Spanish and the choice is the meaning.

segments.text: Para — which way? (At it.) Por — which way? (From it.) And when a sentence takes either? (Both are right — the choice is the meaning.) Next: the two of them in a conversation, where the choice does real work.
